records.quote: The objectives of this investigation were to: (1) determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and (2) investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.
records.derivation: Objective statement, not a statement of the test condition (brief rule 3). The JSON field has a line break (\n) after 'to:'; joined with one space. Source term 'low-gravity'; no g-level stated; mapped to the controlled term microgravity. The 'normal gravity material flammability screening test' is NASA's ground reference test, not a test of PSI-100.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-100/Science Documents/PSI-100_Science Documents_SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III Readme.docx
records.quote: The specific objective of SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III tests is to determine how rapidly a large-scale fire grows in low-gravity and whether it reaches a steady-state spread rate.
records.derivation: Objective statement covering SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III together, not a statement of the test condition. Source term 'low-gravity'; no g-level stated; mapped to the controlled term microgravity. The same sentence, in future tense, is on page 2 of the Objectives PDF ('The objective of the Saffire-I and III tests will be to ...'); not proposed separately because its text layer reads 'lowgravity' across a hyphenated line break.

records.quote: In Saffire-I and –III, the sample material is a single large sample (approx. 0.4 m wide by 0.94 m tall) and demonstrates the development and spread of a large-scale low-gravity fire.
records.derivation: Operational-requirements document specific to SAFFIRE-III, but the sentence covers Saffire-I and -III together and describes what the sample is meant to demonstrate, not a measured test condition. Sentence spans two PDF lines ('0.4 m' / 'wide'), joined with one space. Source term 'low-gravity'; no g-level stated; mapped to the controlled term microgravity.

records.quote: Results determine microgravity flammability limits for several spacecraft materials, help to validate NASA’s material selection criteria, and how microgravity and limited oxygen affect flame size.
records.derivation: Research-impact summary, not a statement of the test condition; no g-level stated. In the PSI-100 record this section opens with 'The Saffire-I experiment provides a new way to study a realistic fire on an exploration vehicle', so the text was written for Saffire-I, and it speaks of 'several spacecraft materials' while section=approach names one material (SIBAL) for Saffire III.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-100/Science Documents/PSI-100_Science Documents_SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf
records.quote: This paper describes the three Spacecraft Fire Experiments (Saffire-I, -II, and -III) that were developed at NASA-GRC and that will conduct a series of material flammability tests in low-gravity and at length scales that are realistic for a spacecraft fire.
records.derivation: Pre-flight paper (future tense 'will conduct'; page 4 Table 4 gives Saffire-III operations as planned for 3-Mar-2017 'as of 4/30/2016'). The sentence covers Saffire-I, -II and -III together. Sentence spans five PDF lines, joined with one space. Source term 'low-gravity' mapped to microgravity.

records.quote: As a follow on to the Saffire 1 investigation, the Saffire III investigation also used SIBAL as the sample material.
records.derivation: Phase inferred from the material name: SIBAL is described in the Readme docx paragraph 3 (R7) as 'a composite fabric consisting of cotton on a fiberglass substrate'; a fabric is a solid. The sentence does not use the word 'solid'.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-100/Science Documents/PSI-100_Science Documents_SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III Readme.docx
records.quote: The sample material for SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III is a composite fabric consisting of cotton on a fiberglass substrate (75% cotton, 25% fiberglass by weight).
records.derivation: Phase inferred from the material form: a cotton-on-fiberglass fabric is a solid; the sentence does not use the word 'solid'. The sentence covers SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III together. The same sentence (with 'Saffire-I and III') is on page 2 of the Objectives PDF.

records.quote: The Saffire-III experiments were performed on the Orbital Science’s Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.
Saffire-III flight system is loaded into the Cygnus PCM and be strapped into place.

records.derivation: section=flightProgram is the PSI flight-program field, not the vehicle where the sample burned. section=approach (R8) says the experiments were performed on the Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS, and the Operations PDF page 1 says 'The Saffire-III experiment begins only after Cygnus is unberthed from the ISS.' Proposed only so the auditor can decide whether this program label may be used as platform. DISCREPANCY not raised: the sources name Cygnus as the vehicle and the ISS as the station it left, without contradiction.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-100/Science Documents/PSI-100_Science Documents_SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf
records.quote: Air is drawn through the flow duct by fans located at the top of the duct with flow straighteners at the bottom of the experiment module.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. The sentence describes the flow duct of the common experiment package (page 2: 'practically all of the hardware would be identical in the three units'), in a pre-flight paper; it is not specific to SAFFIRE-III. No SAFFIRE-III-specific sentence in the sources read names the gas as air, and none states its composition. Sentence spans four PDF lines, joined with one space.

records.source_file: psi-data/PSI-100/Science Documents/PSI-100_Science Documents_SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III Readme.docx
records.quote: SAFFIRE-I will be conducted at an air flow velocity of 20 cm/s while SAFFIRE-III will be run at a flow velocity of 30 cm/s.
records.derivation: air: oxygen balanced mainly by nitrogen. Grammatically 'air' qualifies the SAFFIRE-I flow only; the SAFFIRE-III clause says 'a flow velocity' without naming the gas. Future tense (planning text). The same sentence (with 'Saffire-I' / 'Saffire-III') is on page 2 of the Objectives PDF.

records.quote: Flame spread over a large thin charring surface in low-gravity showed that steady flame spread was possible (unlike normal gravity)
records.derivation: derived: source says 'low-gravity' (orbital free flight in Cygnus). Results slide titled 'Saffire-I-III Results' of Urban et al., ASGSR 2017 (NTRS 20180005168): it covers the three flights together, so it is not independent per flight.

records.quote: Table 1.  Summary of Samples, Test Conditions, and Selected Results [...] Δ %O2 i [...] III-1 Cotton-Fiberglass 40.6 cm 0.37 mm 94 cm 25 cm/s Concurrent 21.2 to 21.0
records.derivation: Table 1 (NTRS 20180005168 page 30) gives '21.2 to 21.0' in column 'Δ %O2 i' for III-1, recorded as the range 21.0-21.2 %O2. The values are absolute O2 percent, not a change. Footnote i is not readable in the text layer. The PSI-99 table carries the same column with the same values as 'Percent O2 (Note 1)', with Note 1 'Derived from measured CO2 production and referenced to initial O2 concentration reported by ISS.' (PSI-99 CSV row=12): a CO2-derived estimate, not a direct O2 sensor reading. The same range is printed for III-2, so it may span the whole Saffire-III run rather than this burn alone. Mapping III-1 -> PSI-100 S1 by flow direction (the only Concurrent sample in each table). The sources conflict on flow speed (NTRS 25 cm/s, PSI-100 table 30 cm/s): do not pair this O2 with the PSI-100 flow value.
records.flag_notes: UNIT_AMBIGUOUS: column header is a change symbol (Δ %O2) while the cells look like absolute percentages. SHARED_LINEAGE: the same table and the same flight hardware design cover Saffire-I, -II and -III (PSI-98, PSI-99, PSI-100).

records.quote: Table 1.  Summary of Samples, Test Conditions, and Selected Results [...] Δ %O2 i [...] III-2 Cotton-Fiberglass 40.6 cm 0.37 mm ~ 10 cm 25 cm/s Opposed 21.2 to 21.0
records.derivation: Table 1 (NTRS 20180005168 page 30) gives '21.2 to 21.0' in column 'Δ %O2 i' for III-2, recorded as the range 21.0-21.2 %O2 (absolute percent). CO2-derived estimate per the matching PSI-99 Note 1; footnote i itself is not readable. Identical to III-1, so it may cover the whole Saffire-III run, and it is the same cabin atmosphere as R501, not an independent observation. Mapping III-2 -> PSI-100 S2 by flow direction (the only Opposed sample in each table); NTRS '~ 10 cm' matches the burned length 3-2 on page 31. The sources conflict on flow speed (NTRS 25 cm/s vs PSI-100 30 cm/s).

not_found.looked_in: Record text, all sections (section=approach only says 'solid state sensors were used to measure pressure, CO2 and O2 mole faction', no value; section=researchImpacts mentions 'limited oxygen', no value). Readme docx paragraphs 1-58 (no ambient O2; '75% cotton, 25% fiberglass by weight' in paragraph 3 is sample composition; Table 2 'Saffire, I, II and III Diagnostics' appears only as a caption, paragraph 27). Objectives PDF pages 1-6: pages 2-3 contain 'just above and below 21% O2 by volume, i.e., the expected concentration of O2 when Cygnus unberths from ISS', but it sits in the Saffire-II material-selection paragraph and is a pre-flight expectation, not a statement of the SAFFIRE-III test atmosphere, so it was not used (would be analogy); Table 2 on page 3 lists 'O2 mole fraction solid-state sensor inlet to avionics bay', no value; 'Elevated O2' in Table 5 on page 5 refers to future Saffire-IV-VI tests. Operations PDF page 1: no O2.

Record text, all sections (section=approach: 'solid state sensors were used to measure pressure'; section=researchImpacts: instruments 'measure oxygen, carbon dioxide, heat, pressure and flame growth'; no value). Readme docx paragraphs 1-58 (no pressure). Objectives PDF pages 1-6 (Table 2 on page 3 lists 'Pressure solid-state sensor in avionics bay', no value; 'lower P' in Table 5 on page 5 refers to future exploration-atmosphere tests, not Saffire-III). Operations PDF page 1 (no pressure).

Not used: section=projectType 'Microgravity Investigation' (category label); section=hypothesis 'There is a significant lack of microgravity data available for spacecraft designers' (motivation, not the test condition); Operations PDF 'The FOT places the Cygnus vehicle into a free-drift mode and initiate the experiment.' (vehicle mode, no gravity stated).

not_found.variable: gravity_regime = normal_gravity (1-g comparison tests run by this investigation)
not_found.looked_in: Record text, Readme docx, Objectives PDF pages 1-6, Operations PDF page 1. None found. The 'normal gravity material flammability screening test' in section=objective is NASA's ground screening test used as a reference (Objectives PDF page 3 names the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 normal-gravity tests and assigns that comparison to Saffire-II), with no test ids in PSI-100.

lineage: Saffire-III shares flight-unit design, sample material and documents with Saffire-I (PSI-98) and Saffire-II (PSI-99). Record section=approach: 'As a follow on to the Saffire 1 investigation, the Saffire III investigation also used SIBAL as the sample material.' Objectives PDF page 2: 'The premise for the design of the flight experiment was that practically all of the hardware would be identical in the three units except possibly for the sample material(s) to be burned.' SIBAL cloth 'was developed for the Solid Inflammability Boundary at Low-Speeds (SIBAL) spaceflight experiment' (Readme paragraph 3). The Readme covers SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III jointly (paragraph 7: 'Table 1. Saffire-I/III Experiment Data in PSI') and paragraph 5 says 'The experiment records are found on the “Data” tab in the SAFFIRE-II Investigations record.' The record's section=researchImpacts opens with 'The Saffire-I experiment provides a new way to study a realistic fire on an exploration vehicle' (text written for Saffire-I). The Objectives PDF was reported by the caller as byte-identical across SAFFIRE I-III (not checked by me). Sample count, for the auditor: the Operations PDF page 1 says 'In Saffire-I and –III, the sample material is a single large sample', while Readme paragraph 3 says 'In addition to the 2 samples' for SAFFIRE-I and SAFFIRE-III together; the sources read do not say which data record (S1, S2) belongs to SAFFIRE-III.
